candidates.rationale: Amihud illiquidity: average price impact per dollar traded; names that move on thin volume are structurally harder to trade and carry a liquidity-risk premium priced as higher expected returns.

Normalized short-vs-long volume divergence (a volume MACD): a burst of near-term trading activity relative to its own baseline signals fresh attention or informed flow that diffuses gradually into price.
Profitable firms (high EPS rank) that also sit high in trailing dollar-volume liquidity draw sustained informed and institutional participation, reinforcing price discovery in quality names.

Under the mixture-of-distributions hypothesis, volume and intraday range are jointly driven by the rate of information arrival; strengthening co-movement flags informed-trading intensity ahead of continued directional moves.

Highly levered firms are most exposed to funding-liquidity shocks; ranking leverage against recent dollar-volume instability isolates firms where balance-sheet fragility and liquidity risk compound into a priced premium.

Rising volume momentum in high book-value-per-share names signals value-driven capital rotation gaining conviction, an attention shock hitting fundamentally-supported stocks that precedes continued re-rating.
Recency-weighted cumulative return scaled by typical trading range separates durable, information-driven price trends from moves that are just range-bound liquidity noise.

Volume aggregated by the sign of daily returns approximates net order-flow imbalance; persistent directional concentration of trading reflects informed accumulation or distribution ahead of continuation.
Today's range relative to its own rolling ceiling flags climactic, liquidity-shock trading days; such extremes tend to mean-revert as liquidity providers step back in and re-tighten spreads.

The share of a month's dollar volume concentrated in its single busiest day measures how event-driven versus steady a stock's liquidity is; lumpy, spike-dominated volume signals unresolved information still diffusing into price.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Range-normalization factors ($high-$low over $dollar_volume, over $open, or via $low/$high min-max) each now have two neighboring windows tried (10&21, 63&126, 21&34); a window-only resubmission of these families will keep hitting archive_subtree or correlation, so change the core transform instead.
  2. Adding an outer TS_DECAY_LINEAR or CS_ZSCORE around an already-archived ratio or z-score expression still shares 9+ nodes with it (3 rejections this round); vary the inner computation, since wrappers alone don't decorrelate.
  3. The accrual_gap x dollar_volume and operating_margin/asset_turnover/leverage families already have close neighbors in the archive: a single added denominator or a rank-subtraction-to-ratio swap scored 0.84-0.86 correlation, not new signal. These need a different combinator, not an arithmetic tweak.
  4. A nested TS_DELTA(TS_MEAN(field,N),N) shape and an overnight-gap x range product (($open - DELAY($close or $high,1)) times ($high-$low)) both collided with alpha101 canonical subtrees regardless of field; avoid re-deriving these two shapes on a new field.
  5. Fundamental CS_RANK crossed multiplicatively with TS_RANK of a price/volume statistic (range, dollar_volume, or its dispersion) produced this round's top 3 fitnesses (3.60, 2.89, 2.20) — extend this template to untried fundamental/window combos before reaching for a CS_ZSCORE-based fusion.
  6. TS_CORR/TS_COV between $return and $volume fails the cheap screen regardless of transform — raw, SIGN, and ABS variants all scored |t| 0.36-0.71 this round. Don't propose return-volume co-movement statistics directly; rank one leg first or drop the raw return leg.
  7. A 1-day TS_DELTA on a fundamental (e.g. $roe) fails the coverage gate (0.784-0.786) even though that fundamental's level is normally reliable. Treat short-window fundamental deltas as a coverage risk, not just a signal-flatness risk.
  8. Swapping $volume for $dollar_volume doesn't decorrelate even when buried inside a larger fusion (rho 0.986 under a CS_RANK*TS_RANK wrapper) or when only the denominator's statistic changes (rho 0.919, raw dollar_volume vs its own TS_STD). Check the archive under both fields before submitting either.
  9. Changing only the outer time-series statistic (e.g. TS_STD vs TS_MEAN) on an otherwise-identical guarded ratio still collides on archive_subtree (7 shared nodes this round) — the inner expression needs to change too, not just the outer wrapper.
  10. The 'difference of two CS_RANK((high-low)/(X+eps))' family with a 5-day normalizer window is archive-saturated — two independent proposals this round shared 5 and 10 nodes with existing accepts. Retire this exact shape or move to a materially longer window.
  11. Of all $return-based cheap_screen rejects this round, a 40-day return sum normalized by 21-day range came closest to clearing (|t| 0.82) — a decayed or reweighted version of that specific pairing is worth one more try before dropping return-sum-over-range ideas entirely.
  12. Several within-round duplicates reused the same 5-day dollar_volume/range ratio and the same-length roa/roe delta shape — vary window length or operator before resubmitting a shape already tried earlier in the same run.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
Leave `parent_ids` empty and `changed_node` empty for EXPLORE.
